correctness.rationale: In the unrolled sparse regime the parallel exclusion rule is P_i(t+1)=min(P_i(t)+1,P_{i+1}(t)−1). Subtracting t+2i yields a sliding minimum of initial B_i=p_i−2i, whose drift over k particles is n−2k≥0. At t=k−1 the appended endpoint cannot lower the old minimum, so every empty-cell gap is at least one. At t=k−2 a zero gap occurs exactly when the added endpoint is strictly below the entire old window; its drop is at most one because B increments are ≥−1. Two such records would force B_(ell+k)<B_(ell')<B_ell for ell<ell'<ell+k, contradicting the drift. In reverse gap order the record condition is that the first q gaps sum to at most q−1. A bijection with Dyck paths writes each gap as that many down-steps followed by one up-step, then appends down-steps until the height is zero; the nonnegative condition just before each up-step is the displayed inequality. The omitted physical gap is set by the hole count and is at least two, so each choice of record particle site and Catalan path gives one distinct labeled input. For k=1 all n sparse states are already relaxed, and at half filling gap separation forces alternation. Complement-reflection commutes with the update and handles the dense bound and census. The source verifier and its recorded run were inspected; the general argument is analytic.
residual_risks: The unique adjacent-ones-pair statement is scoped to 2≤k≤n/2. The uploaded checker detects the existence of a near-final blockage from relaxation time rather than separately counting the number of actual adjacent pairs; uniqueness is justified by the proof.

evidence: A qualifying window at time t has length 2t+2 and positive even terminal height, so contains at least t+2 particles. Both windows used here fit on the ring when 2k≤n. At t=k−1 there are no such windows. At t=k−2 each contains exactly k particles and has endpoint height two.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: There cannot be two qualifying backward window starts: each start is a particle and is contained in the other window since each window contains all k particles. The two backward arcs from one start up to but excluding the other are then both nonempty proper prefixes of admissible windows, so have positive height sums; together they cover the cycle, of sum 2k−n≤0. Thus counting the n positioned windows times the prior Catalan count counts distinct extremizers. The prefixes just before the second through kth particles give exactly the inequalities sum of the first q backward gaps ≤q−1. Conversely those inequalities place all k particles in the window and keep every prefix positive (after the kth particle, the all-hole remainder ends at height two). This proves the classified strict record as well. Complement-reflection and the single-particle case finish every stated parameter.

evidence: For a walk of length 2t starting at height two and ending at y, the prior count is N_(2t,y−2)−N_(2t,y+2), with N_(a,b)=binom(a,(a+b)/2). At y=2 this is binom(2t,t)−binom(2t,t+2)=C_(t+1). Both later Resultary records print n C_(m−1).
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: For time t=k−2 at fixed sparse mass k, y=2 is the only possible final height of an admissible length-2k−2 window; no exterior particles remain to choose. The exact count per cyclic position is therefore a specialization of the existing formula, not a new table.

originality.rationale: Fukś's earlier local preimage theorem and exact ballot count already imply the fixed-mass sharp bound, labeled Catalan census and unique final blockage, including the stated initial strict gap-record characterization. This is concrete prior implication, not just reuse of a general technique, nor a priority inference from the later catalogue matches. The min-plus proof is an alternate derivation of a mechanically covered claim.

value.rationale: Worst-case time and first extremal multiplicity are naturally motivated for synchronous traffic. But the exact invariant here reduces to evaluating the published preimage count at its smallest possible height, together with one additive cyclic prefix argument. The min-plus reformulation reads well as an alternate proof; it does not supply a separate unknown or non-mechanically-implied scientific invariant of the system.
residual_risks: The negative assessment is about a distinct scientific contribution in this record, not about the usefulness of the traffic question or its exposition.
